lawyer:
Md. Awlad Ali, Advocate  -------- For the Appellant. 
Syed Amirul Islam, Advocate  -------- For the Respondent.
parties:
Abdul Karim   -------- Appellant.
Vs.
Shamsul Alam   -------- Respondent.
full_judgment:
Kazi Ebadul Hoque, J. : This appeal by the complainant under section 417(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is against judgment of acquittal dated 15.6.86 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Criminal Appeal No. 91 of 1986 setting, aside the conviction of the respondent No. 1 Shamsul Alam under section 420 of the Penal Code and sentence of six months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Tk. 5000.00, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for two months imposed by judgment dated 9.3.86 passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in Petition Case No. 6a/85/48. 

 2. Prosecution case, in short, is that the complainant PW 1 Abdul Karim deals in motor pumps at 98, Nawabpur Road, Dhaka under the name and style of Holly Machinery Store as distributors whole and retail sellers. Accused Shamsul Alam is an importer of motor pumps having his shop at 28, Nawabpur Road, Dhaka under the name and style of Shams Trading Company and used to deliver the imported motor pumps to the complainant for sale. On the assurance of delivering 200 pieces of motor pumps, accused received total sum of Tk. 6,04,050.00 from the complainant in different, installments beginning from 12.4.85 and then on 30.4.85, 27.6.85 and lastly on 24.7.85 and acknowledged the same in writing on a sheet of his printed pad Ext. 1 and promised to deliver the motor pumps within 3 days from 24.7.85. Complainant also paid the sum of Tk. 99,050.00 to the accused on that date on account of his past dues for which the accused granted a receipt-Ext, 2. The accused having not delivered the said goods within the agreed period of 3 days, complainant on inquiry came to learn on 12.8.85 that the accused had been staying in a hotel at Chittagong and he sent his son PW 3 Mizanur Rahman to Chittagong. PW 3 and complainant's brother-in-law PW 2 Sakhawat Hossain, a businessman of Chittagong traced out the accused on 13.8.85 in a hotel at Chittagong and the accused promised to deliver the motor pumps on 14.8.85. On that date the accused having not been found in the Chittagong Port by PWs 2 and 3 on inquiry they came to learn on 15.8.85 that the imported motor pumps were being sent through M/s. Shawket Transport. The said goods were seized with the help of police of Double mooring police station. Thereafter complainant filed the complaint case before the Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on 25.8.85. The complainant, therefore, prayed for recovery of the said goods and punishment of the accused for cheating. 

 3. Defence of the accused is that he is innocent and the complainant has filed the case against him on false allegation to put pressure upon him to deliver the imported motor pumps without paying the enhanced price of the same due to increase of duties and taxes. His further defence is that he is a registered importer of motor pumps and had been carrying on business with the complainant since 1982. He having no show room or sale centre he used to sell his imported motor pumps through the complainant's shop by delivering the same in Dhakaand there was no agreement to deliver any motor pump to the complainant in Chittagong. Due to failure of the complainant to pay the advance money in spite of repeated demands by the accused though the motor pumps reached Chittagong port in April, 1985 the same could, not be cleared from the port in time. In the meantime Custom Duty having increased from 50% to 100% and 10% regularatory duty having also been imposed with effect from 1.7.85 on receipt of some amount of money on 24th of July, 1985 from the complainant the accused went to Chittagong to clear the goods and booked the same with the Shawkat Transport Agency for delivery to his firm Shams Trading Company in Dhaka. Thereafter complainant with the help of police of Doublemooring PS on false allegation seized 198 pieces of motor pumps. He denied that he never agreed to sell the said pumps at the alleged rate and the same was never written under his instruction by PW 5 Santosh Kumar Shaha; ruther the said false rate was entered from a previous sale receipt by forgery. The alleged transaction with the complainant was in course of bonafide business of the accused and there was no intention of cheating on his part. But the complainant out of greed and for wrongful gain filed the false case against the accused. 

 9. Though the appellant in his petition of complaint stated that the accused received money from him on condition of delivering to him 200 pieces of domestic pumps at Chittagong port no such evidence has been adduced by him in the dock as PW 1. Court of appeal below noticed from the evidence of PW 4 Abdul Jalil, an employee of the appellant that the agreement was to deliver motor pumps in Dhaka as it was the previous practice. In such circumstances clearing motor pumps by the accused from Chittagong port and booking the same through Shawkat Transport Agency to his own address in Dhaka cannot be said to be an attempt on the part of the accused to deceive him from getting delivery of the same in Dhaka. It is in evidence that before the case in question was filed the said goods were seized by the police of Doublemooring PS on the complaint of PW 2 Sakhawat Hossain, brother-in-law of the appellant when the practice was always to deliver the goods to the appellant in Dhaka by the accused. Time for delivering the same did not arise when the goods were simply booked from Chittagong for onward transmission to Dhaka. Thus it cannot also be said that the subsequent conduct of the accused was fraudulent as found by the trial Court. Therefore, we find no illegality in the finding of the court of appeal below that no malafide intention of the accused was revealed from clearing the goods by the accused. 

 11. Court of appeal below noticed that the rate of the price mentioned in Ext. 1 was not written by PW 5 Santosh Kumar Shaha under instruction of the accused. PW 5 admitted in cross-examination that the rate mentioned in the receipt dated 22.8.84 Ext. A has similarity with the rate mentioned in Ext. 1. The accused denied that PW 5 wrote the said rate under his instruction; rather his contention is that the said rate was copied subsequently from Ext. A lying with the complainant. Admittedly customs duty was raised from 50% to 100% with effect from 1st of July, 1985 and the goods were cleared on 15.8.85. PW 2 stated in his deposition that after the goods were seized by the police he went to the residence of customs auditor Abdul Karim and talked with the accused who informed him that he was not delivering the goods due to enhancement of price of the goods. We have already found that there was no agreement to deliver the goods at Chittagong. In the circumstances seizing the goods at Chittagong before the time to deliver the same in Dhaka arose and filing the criminal case subsequently on 25.8.85 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka was only to put undue pressure on the accused to part with the goods at a lesser price.
